scope: scripts/qualify_opcua_changes.py from commit 60efc26 on one owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 (TIA V21 Update 3): the three server-interface kinds and opcua_role_mapping_set (standard roles Operator with a project role and Observer without one, then removal of Operator), each prepared, applied with checkpoint, compile and save, read back with untouched peers, reopened in a fresh Portal and restored from its checkpoint, plus typed refusals and opcua_engineering_export of the whole server and each interface. Role restores are compared after a fresh Portal opens the recovered copy.
limitations: One owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 with the OPC UA server on and the Small runtime license; other CPUs and licenses are not exercised.
Server interfaces hold authored objects without PLC variable mappings (fixtures/opcua/server-interface-v1.xml and -v2.xml); mapped variables, methods and SiOME exports are not imported.

opcua_role_mapping_set maps the standard roles Operator (with a project role) and Observer (without one). V21 creates custom roles only in the namespace of a SIMATIC server interface, which no change kind creates; a custom role elsewhere is refused before anything is written.
opcua_engineering_export: the whole-server export and each server interface; SIMATIC interfaces and reference namespaces are empty in a scratch.

V21 Update 3: ReferenceNamespaces.Create terminates TIA ("Unexpected exception", Portal disposed) for every NodeSet tried, including the OPC Foundation DI 1.05.0 NodeSet, headless and with TIA's user interface, with the OPC UA server on or off (29 October 2026); this run reproduces it last with fixtures/opcua/machine-v1.xml.
Interface lastModified times are not compared: importing one interface moves the others' times; content is compared by export hash.

TIA derives the interface namespace's row in the namespace access restrictions and in every role mapping from the interface: it appears on import and vanishes on delete, and a copy recovered from a checkpoint lacks it until TIA rebuilds it; those rows are not compared.

TIA caches OPC UA role mappings per Portal process, keyed by an object id a recovered copy keeps: the Portal that restored a role change shows the mappings from before the restore. Role restores are therefore compared after a fresh Portal opens the recovered copy, and the worker refuses OPC UA changes in the restoring Portal (StaleRevision).
Engineering only; nothing is downloaded and no OPC UA client connects.
